meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future with AI math while the rest of the supply chain burns to the ground.

cooking.headline: AI just solved a math problem that would take a human ten lifetimes
cooking.summary: AI has finally cracked a major mathematical mystery, proving that if you give a computer enough compute, it will eventually do your homework better than you ever could. At least now when we fail our math exams, we can blame the machine for making the answer too hard to understand.
cooking.plain_english: An artificial intelligence system has successfully solved a complex, long-standing problem in the field of mathematics.

cooking.headline: OpenComputer is the open source answer to your AI coding agent addiction
cooking.summary: We finally have an open-source alternative to Devin, because apparently, we haven't automated enough of our own jobs yet. It's the perfect tool for when you want your computer to hallucinate bugs at a speed only a machine can match.
cooking.plain_english: OpenComputer is a free, publicly available software tool designed to act as an automated assistant for writing and managing computer code.

cooking.headline: Zero C# lets you escape the garbage collector, just like your landlord escapes maintenance requests
cooking.summary: Someone decided C# is way too comfortable and stripped out the runtime and garbage collector entirely. It's a bold move to manually manage your own memory in 2026, but hey, at least you can finally blame yourself when it crashes.
cooking.plain_english: Zero C# is a tool that allows developers to write and run C# code without relying on the standard software framework or automatic memory management systems.

cooked.headline: Anthropic's IPO is the latest sign that the AI bubble is leaking air
cooked.summary: Anthropic tried to go public during a massive market cooling, proving that even the smartest AI models can't predict a brutal Wall Street vibe check. Turns out, investors are finally realizing that burning billions in GPU costs isn't exactly a sustainable business model.
cooked.plain_english: Anthropic's initial public offering performed poorly as part of a wider decline in the market value of artificial intelligence companies.

cooked.headline: The FBI's criminal database might have been hacked, which is the ultimate 'who watches the watchmen' moment.
cooked.summary: The agency tasked with catching the world's most sophisticated hackers reportedly got their own database compromised by an intruder. It turns out that even the people who write the security playbooks can still fall for a classic phishing expedition.
cooked.plain_english: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating a potential security breach of its internal criminal records system.

cooked.headline: An RCE vulnerability in GnuPG is the security equivalent of finding a hole in your front door's deadbolt.
cooked.summary: We rely on GnuPG to keep our most sensitive communications locked away, but this bug basically hands the keys to anyone with a malicious file. It is a harsh reminder that the tools we trust to save us are just as prone to spaghetti code as everything else.
cooked.plain_english: A critical security vulnerability has been discovered in GnuPG that allows an attacker to execute unauthorized commands on a user's computer.

cooked.headline: Nvidia is finding out that accounting is harder than training LLMs
cooked.summary: The SEC is poking around Nvidia's books, which is exactly the kind of side quest no one wants during a historic bull run. It turns out that when you start making more money than some countries, people eventually stop asking about your GPU benchmarks and start asking about your spreadsheets.

cooked.headline: Our AI supply chain is basically a group project where no one checked their code
cooked.summary: AI tools are leaking user data because the underlying supply chain is held together by duct tape and blind optimism. It is the digital equivalent of submitting a final project where you accidentally left your API keys in the public repo.
cooked.plain_english: Security researchers have found that vulnerabilities in the software supply chains used to build AI systems are frequently exposing sensitive user information.

cooked.headline: OpenRouter prompts may have been exposed, proving privacy is just a suggestion
cooked.summary: Users discovered that their sensitive prompts sent to Minimax via OpenRouter were potentially readable by unauthorized parties. It turns out the 'cloud' is really just someone else's computer where your private data is currently on a public reading tour.
cooked.plain_english: OpenRouter users reported that prompts sent to the Minimax model may have been accessible to unauthorized individuals.

cooked.headline: Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains, officially ending the year's vibe check
cooked.summary: The market spent all year climbing a mountain only to realize it forgot its wallet at the trailhead. If your portfolio is currently tracking at zero, at least you can say you've reached a state of perfect, tax-neutral zen.
cooked.plain_english: The Nasdaq stock index has declined to the level it was at the beginning of 2026, meaning all gains for the year have been lost.
